text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has to win back its credibility in organising a fair general elections.
- Cherif Rahmani, special minister for Algiers city administration, says the decision to ban vehicle stopping in main streets and places was "a difficult and painful one".
- Said Saadi, leader of the Rally for Culture and Democrcay (RCD) party, presides over a meeting of solidarity with Algeria in Paris.
- Security forces dismantle a 19-member network of the Algerian Djihad Islamic Front (FIDA) in Algiers.

- Nine family members were slaughtered on Monday-Tuesday night in a rebel raid in Benchicao hamlet, 10 km (five miles) from Medea where 31 people were hacked to death in a similar attack last week. Security forces kill 25 "terriorists" in Chlef and dimantle an armed gang of 19 in Aligers.
- Spending spree on clothes ahead of Aid el Fitr, marking the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
